title: A nonsingular square matrix over a DVR is equivalent to a nonzero diagonal matrix
statement: Let A be a commutative integral domain that is a discrete valuation ring. For every m ∈ ℕ and square matrix D indexed by Fin m over A with det(D) ≠ 0, there exist square matrices P and Q invertible under matrix multiplication and a function d : Fin m → A such that every d(i) is nonzero and P D Q = diagonal(d). No ordering or divisibility condition on consecutive diagonal entries is asserted.
lean_statement: ∀ (A : Type*) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [IsDiscreteValuationRing A] (m : ℕ) (D : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) A), D.det ≠ 0 → ∃ (P Q : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) A) (d : Fin m → A), IsUnit P ∧ IsUnit Q ∧ (∀ i, d i ≠ 0) ∧ P * D * Q = Matrix.diagonal d
